en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Third Chapter
The Discussion on the Faculties of the Eighth-Rank Person: Is it the case that the eighth-rank person lacks the faculty of faith?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that the person who is an eighth-rank individual lacks faith?
One should certainly not say so.
Is it not the case that the person who is an eighth-rank individual lacks the faculty of energy? ... [and so on] ... one should certainly not say so.
Is there no faculty of mindfulness …pe… is there no faculty of concentration …pe… is there no faculty of wisdom?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does the person who is at the eighth stage (aṭṭhamaka) lack wisdom?
You should not say so …pe….
Does the person who is an eighth-level practitioner possess faith? Yes.
Does the person who is an eighth-level practitioner possess the faculty of faith?
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … for the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner, there is energy … there is mindfulness …
Is there concentration?
Is there wisdom? Yes.
Does the person who is an eighth-level practitioner possess the faculty of wisdom?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Does the person who is an eighth-level practitioner possess the mind, and does he possess the faculty of mind?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess faith? Does he possess the faculty of faith?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess mind? Does he possess the mind-faculty?
Yes. Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess wisdom? Does he possess the wisdom-faculty?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does the person who is an eighth-level practitioner possess mental joy? Does he possess the faculty of mental joy? Does he possess life? Does he possess the faculty of life?
Yes.
Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess faith? Does he possess the faculty of faith?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess life? Does he possess the life-faculty?
“Yes.
“Does a person who is an eighth-rank individual possess wisdom?
Does he possess the faculty of wisdom?”
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess faith, yet lack the faculty of faith?
Yes.
Does the person who is at the eighth stage possess the mind, but not the mind-faculty?
One should certainly not say so… [and so on] … Does the person who is at the eighth stage possess faith, but not the faith-faculty?
“Yes,” [you reply].
“Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess mental joy, yet lack the faculty of mental joy? …pe… “Does he possess life, yet lack the faculty of life?
You should not say so …pe…
Does the person who is an eighth-level practitioner possess wisdom, yet lack the faculty of wisdom?
Yes. Does the person who is an eighth-level practitioner possess the mind, yet lack the faculty of mind? Yes.
Is there mental joy, but no faculty of mental joy?
Is there life, but no faculty of life?
One should certainly not say so… [and so on].
Is it not the case that the person who is an eighth-rank individual lacks the faculty of faith?
Yes, it is.
Is such an eighth-rank individual devoid of faith?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that the eighth person lacks the faculty of energy?
Yes, it is.
Is the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner (aṭṭhamaka) one who is indolent and of inferior energy?
One should not say so …pe… Does the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner lack the faculty of mindfulness (satindriya)?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner (aṭṭhamaka) one who is forgetful and lacking clear comprehension?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is it not the case that the person who is an eighth-rank individual lacks the faculty of concentration?
Yes, it is.
Is such an eighth-rank individual unconcentrated and of wandering mind?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does the person who is at the eighth stage lack the faculty of wisdom? Yes.
Is the person who is an eighth-rank individual one who is witless and like a water-buffalo?
One should not say so … [as before] … Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess faith, and is that faith leading to liberation?
“Yes.
“If there is faith in a person who has reached the eighth stage, and that faith is conducive to liberation, then indeed, it should not be said:
‘A person who has reached the eighth stage lacks the faculty of faith.’”
In the person who has reached the eighth stage, there is energy, and that energy is leading to liberation;
there is mindfulness, and that mindfulness is leading to liberation;
there is concentration, and that concentration is leading to liberation.
"There is wisdom, and that wisdom is leading to liberation"? Yes.
If there is wisdom for the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner, and that wisdom is leading to liberation, then indeed, it should not be said: [that the path is not yet fully developed].
“It is said: ‘The person who is at the eighth stage has no faculty of wisdom.
Does the person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning have faith? Does he have the faculty of faith?”—“Yes.”
Does the person who is a candidate for the fruit of the eighth stage possess faith? Does he possess the faculty of faith?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Does the person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning possess wisdom? Does he possess the faculty of wisdom?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess wisdom? Does he possess the faculty of wisdom?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Does a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning...
a person who is practicing for the realization of arhatship possess faith, possess the faculty of faith... [and so on]...
possess wisdom, possess the faculty of wisdom?
“Yes.
“But does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess wisdom? Does he possess the faculty of wisdom?
“One should not say so” … [and so on] …
Does the person who is a candidate for the eighth stage possess faith, yet lack the faculty of faith?
Yes.
Does the person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning possess faith, yet lack the faculty of faith?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does the person who is an eighth-rank individual possess wisdom, yet lack the faculty of wisdom?
Yes.
"One who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning possesses wisdom, yet does not possess the faculty of wisdom"?
One should not say this... [and so on] ...
"The person who is an eighth-rank practitioner possesses faith, yet does not possess the faculty of faith"... [and so on].
"There is wisdom, but there is no faculty of wisdom"? Yes.
[Is this true] for a person who has entered upon the practice for the realization of the fruit of non-returning? ...
Is it not the case that for a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship, wisdom exists, yet the faculty of wisdom does not exist?
One should certainly not say so… [and so on]… Does the eighth-person (the *aṣṭamaka*) lack the five faculties?
"Yes.
"But was it not said by the Blessed One:
'Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties'?"
Which five? The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom—
these, monks, are the five faculties.
"Monks, it is through the fulfillment and perfection of these five faculties that one becomes an arahant.
With faculties weaker than those, one is practicing for the realization of arahantship; with faculties weaker than those, one is a non-returner;
with faculties weaker than those, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning; with faculties weaker than those, one is a once-returner."
When they are weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning;
when they are weaker than that, one is a stream-enterer; when they are weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry.
Monks, I say of anyone who lacks these five faculties entirely, in every way, and in all respects, that they are an outsider, standing on the side of the worldlings.”
Is that indeed the Sutta?
Yes. Is it stated that the person who is an eighth-rank individual stands outside, on the side of the worldlings? Yes.
It should not be stated thus...
[as before] ...therefore, the eightfold person possesses the five faculties.
The discussion on the faculties of the eighth person is concluded.
